title: Add readiness-suite benchmark mode for new Dedicated pools (pass/fail + summary JSON)
author: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Context: Provision-to-ready automation needs a fast, deterministic “is this pool healthy enough to hand to routing?” gate. Our existing perf-canary runs are too heavy for brand-new pools (long runtime, lots of knobs, and outputs that are hard for the provisioning pipeline to interpret).

This PR introduces a new benchmark mode: readiness-suite.

What it does: Adds `--mode readiness-suite` (alias `--suite readiness`) that runs a small fixed set of smoke+perf probes designed for freshly provisioned Dedicated pools. It validates basic inference viability, catches the most common misconfigurations (bad networking/TLS, broken model pull, CUDA/runtime issues), and provides a minimal performance signal without requiring full benchmarking.

Output contract: In readiness-suite mode we always emit a single summary JSON (to stdout by default, or to a file via `--output-json <path>`). The summary includes: overall pass/fail, exit code semantics, per-test status, and a small set of metrics used by the provisioner gate. The goal is to make the pipeline integration dead simple: run command, parse JSON, mark stage passed/failed, attach the JSON blob to the provisioning run.

Runtime: ~2–4 minutes on a typical new pool node (after model is available locally). Model caching is respected; if the model is missing, we fail fast with an actionable error and a distinct failure code.

Key details:
- Adds a readiness suite runner with three phases: (1) environment sanity (GPU visible, driver/CUDA versions, disk space), (2) functional smoke (single request + streaming request against the configured endpoint/adapter), (3) minimal perf sample (short token generation run with fixed prompt/params; collects latency p50/p95, tokens/sec, error rate).
- Thresholds are intentionally conservative; they’re not meant to rank pools, only to catch “clearly broken” capacity. Defaults are documented and can be tuned via `--readiness-thresholds <path>` but the provisioning pipeline should rely on defaults unless there’s a region/SKU exception.
- Adds stable exit codes for the pipeline: 0 = PASS, 10 = FAIL_THRESHOLD (functional ok but perf below threshold), 11 = FAIL_FUNCTIONAL (request errors), 12 = FAIL_ENV (GPU/runtime/env failure), 13 = FAIL_CONFIG (invalid flags/config).
- Adds a schema doc for the emitted JSON and a golden test fixture to prevent accidental breaking changes.

Example:
`perf-canary --mode readiness-suite --target https://10.0.0.12:8443 --model llama-3.1-8b-instruct --output-json /tmp/readiness.json`

Example JSON (abbreviated): `{ "mode":"readiness-suite", "pass":true, "exit_code":0, "suite_version":"2025-02-12", "target":"https://…", "model":"llama-3.1-8b-instruct", "metrics":{"latency_ms_p50":180, "latency_ms_p95":420, "tokens_per_sec":115.2, "error_rate":0.0}, "tests":[{"name":"gpu_visible","status":"pass"},{"name":"smoke_generate","status":"pass"},{"name":"perf_sample","status":"pass"}] }`

Why in perf-canary (vs provisioning service): Keeps the benchmark logic, model invocation, and performance measurement in the tool that already understands our inference adapters. The provisioning pipeline can treat it as a black box.

Notes / compatibility:
- Existing modes are unchanged.
- The readiness JSON schema is additive-only; changes require updating the golden fixture test.
- The default readiness model is NOT hard-coded; callers must specify `--model` (provisioner will pass the pool’s configured “pinned” model).

Follow-ups:
- Add SKU-specific threshold presets once we collect enough baseline (tracked in ENG-2756 for backfill + distributions).
- Consider emitting a small text summary for operators in addition to JSON (kept out of this PR to avoid muddying the pipeline contract).
commits: cli: add readiness-suite mode and stable exit codes
suites: implement environment sanity + smoke + perf sample probes
output: add readiness summary JSON + schema doc
tests: add golden JSON fixture + exit code tests
docs: update README with readiness-suite usage for provisioning pipeline
conversation: Vanessa Ortiz: This is exactly the shape we need for the provision-to-ready gate. Two questions: (1) can we guarantee JSON is printed even on failure? (2) can you add a correlation_id field so the orchestration service can stitch logs together?

Rina Kobayashi (author): (1) yes — readiness-suite always writes a summary JSON; on hard config parse errors we still emit a minimal JSON with pass=false + exit_code=13. (2) added optional `--correlation-id` passthrough; included in JSON and logs.

Rafael Mendes: Exit codes look good. Please ensure FAIL_THRESHOLD only happens when functional tests pass; we don’t want a slow endpoint to mask a broken TLS handshake and end up categorized incorrectly.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Updated categorization order: env -> functional -> threshold. FAIL_THRESHOLD is only returned if env+functional probes pass and perf metrics are below threshold.
Logan Wright: Metric names should align with the time-to-ready dashboards. Can you rename `tps` to `tokens_per_sec` and `p95_ms` to `latency_ms_p95` for clarity/consistency?
Rina Kobayashi (author): Done; updated schema + golden fixture; kept old names out entirely since this is a new mode.

Miles Thornton: Multi-region note: the model download step can be slow/blocked; please make sure the suite fails fast if model isn’t local rather than waiting 15 minutes and timing out the provisioning stage.

Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `--model-fetch-policy=fail-if-missing` default for readiness-suite (overridable). The error message points to the imaging/bootstrap stages and includes the missing artifact ID when available.
Vanessa Ortiz: Requested changes: document default thresholds and why they’re conservative; also add a field for suite_version so we can track changes over time in metrics.
Rina Kobayashi (author): Added `suite_version` string in JSON and documented thresholds in README + schema description.
Rafael Mendes: Approved after re-run; CI is green and the failure mode mapping looks sane.
Vanessa Ortiz: Approved. Please link this in the provision-to-ready runbook once it lands.
merge_summary: Merged readiness-suite benchmark mode with stable exit codes and summary JSON output for provisioning readiness gates.
release_notes: perf-canary: Added `--mode readiness-suite` to run a fast readiness benchmark for new pools and emit a single pass/fail JSON summary with stable exit codes for automation.
